newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends firm as banks sell dollars.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends firm as banks sell dollars.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed firm against the greenback on Thursday which saw banks unload dollars they had accumulated over the past few days, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.45 to the dollar after opening at 58.48. On Wednesday also it had closed at 58.45, dealers said.
"There was some import covering which pushed the dollar up to the 58.54 level. Then the sellers came in," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.

Other dealers said banks, which had accumulated dollar positions when the U.S. currency stagnated during the past several days, were looking to unload their holdings the moment the dollar saw a slight increase.
The rush to shed dollars saw the rupee pick up slightly in the afternoon, which ended at 58.45, they said.
Overnight call money, which opened at 12.5 percent, closed at 11.75 percent with the market liquid, dealers said.
The forex market will be closed on Friday due to a Buddhist holiday.
